facts.statement: The genus Hulkepholis contains two species: the type species H. willetti and H. plotos.
facts.quote: It contains two species, the type species, Hulkepholis willetti, and also H. plotos.

facts.statement: The holotype of H. willetti was collected by Edgar W. Willett at Cuckfield, West Sussex, from Valanginian-aged strata.
facts.quote: It was collected by Edgar W. Willett at Cuckfield, West Sussex, from the Valanginian-aged Grinstead Clay Member, of the Hastings Group, Wealden Supergroup.

facts.statement: Although considered lost by the research community, the holotype of H. willetti was found to be safely accessioned at the Booth Museum in Brighton.
facts.quote: The specimen was considered lost among the crocodyliform research community but was actually safely accessioned at the Booth Museum in Brighton.

facts.statement: Salisbury and Naish assigned the specimen to the new species Goniopholis willetti in 2011, honoring its collector.
facts.quote: It was assigned to a new species of Goniopholis, Goniopholis willetti, by Salisbury and Naish in 2011 honoring its collector.

facts.statement: Buscalioni et al. reassigned the species to its own genus in 2013, creating the new combination Hulkepholis willetti.
facts.quote: Thus it was reassigned to its own genus by Buscalioni et al. (2013), creating the combinatio nova, Hulkepholis willetti.

facts.statement: The genus name Hulkepholis honors John Whitaker Hulke, who originally described the specimen.
facts.quote: The generic name honors John Whitaker Hulke who described the specimen as belonging to Goniopholis.

facts.statement: The species H. plotos was first described and named by Buscalioni, Alcalá, Espílez, and Mampel in 2013.
facts.quote: A second species, Hulkepholis plotos, was first described and named by A.D. Buscalioni, L. Alcalá, E. Espílez and L. Mampel in 2013.

facts.statement: The specific name plotos is derived from the Greek word for 'drifter'.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Greek mythology πλοτός, plotos, the drifter.

facts.statement: H. plotos is known solely from a partial skeleton holotype consisting of a crushed skull, three vertebrae, a rib, a metapodial, and three osteoderms.
facts.quote: It is known solely from the holotype AR-1/56, a partial skeleton which consists of AR-1-2045, a nearly complete but crushed skull; AR-1-2048, 4859, 4860, three vertebrae; AR-1-2046, a rib; AR-1-2048, a metapodial; and AR-1-2049, 4861, 4862, three osteoderms.

facts.statement: The holotype of H. plotos was collected from the early Albian-aged Escucha Formation at Santa Maria Mine in Ariño, Teruel Province, alongside the related species Anteophthalmosuchus escuchae.
facts.quote: It was collected from the early Albian-aged Escucha Formation, at Santa Maria Mine located in the municipality of Ariño, Teruel Province, of Aragon, along with the closely related Anteophthalmosuchus escuchae.

facts.statement: Hulkepholis lived from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, approximately 137.05 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Hulkepholis is an extinct mesoeucrocodylian belonging to the family Goniopholididae that lived in the Escucha Formation in Ariño, Teruel, Spain.
facts.quote: Hulkepholis es un género extinto de mesoeucrocodilio perteneciente a la familia de los goniofolídidos que vivió durante el Cretácico Inferior en la Formación Escucha (principios de la etapa del Albiense) en Ariño, en la provincia de Teruel, en Aragón, al este de España.

facts.statement: The species H. plotos is known exclusively from holotype AR-1-2045, which consists of a nearly complete but crushed skull.
facts.quote: Es conocido exclusivamente a partir del fósil holotipo AR-1-2045 el cual consiste en un cráneo casi completo aunque aplastado.
